title: Hardware-backed key lifecycle operator and secrets-sync bridge for VPC private deployments
creator: Alex Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform-backed operator (TF module + small controller) that manages lifecycle of hardware-backed keys and provides a bidirectional secrets synchronization bridge between cloud Secrets Manager and Vault for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. Goals: 1) enable customers in VPC/private installs to use HSM-backed key material with clear upgrade paths, 2) provide an optional secrets-sync bridge to mirror operational secrets (certs, DB creds, runtime config) from a cloud secrets store into a local Vault instance with envelope-wrapping keys stored in the HSM, and 3) expose automated healthchecks and remediation hooks for SRE/ops. This ticket covers module API, upgrade and drift strategy, health probes (kube and non-kube flavors), basic controller to rotate/replicate keys, and integration tests + docs required for a Customer Private deployment runbook.
acceptance_criteria: TF module exposes a stable input surface for key providers: hsm_config, cloud_kms_arn, vault_addr, secrets_manager_config
Module provisions HSM key assets (or imports existing key handles) and stores metadata in a lock/state asset; no raw key material is written to state
A lightweight controller (helm chart) implements secrets-sync modes: pull-only, push-only, and continuous-sync with conflict resolution rules
Healthchecks: k8s liveness/readiness endpoints for controller, plus non-k8s probe scripts that return structured status and remediation hints
Upgrade plan demonstrates a safe key rotation/dual-write canary path with rollback steps and automated smoke tests
End-to-end integration tests in staging that exercise import, rotation, sync, and failover run green
Documentation and runbook added (Confluence + example TF usage) and security review approved
design_decisions: Prefer an opinionated TF module + optional Kubernetes controller (Helm) to keep IaC declarative and runtime responsibilities small
Do not persist unencrypted key material in Terraform state; use remote secret store references and a keystore abstraction
Secrets-sync should prefer vault as authoritative in case of conflict when configured; allow configurable conflict policy per-secret path
Support both cloud-managed KMS (for customers who use cloud KMS) and HSM-attached modules for air-gapped customers
Expose metrics (Prometheus) and structured logs for observability; healthchecks should include dependency checks (HSM reachability, Vault auth, network egress)
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy TF module in staging with import=false and sync disabled. 2) Validate HSM connectivity and metadata-only state. 3) Enable secrets-sync in pull-only mode, run smoke checks. 4) Enable continuous sync with low RPS, monitor Prometheus alerts for error/sync-lag >30s. 5) Canary key rotation on single tenant, run functional tests. 6) Gradual ramp to production cluster scale. Rollback: disable sync, revert TF change and run a vault re-seed from snapshot snapshot-<timestamp>.
upgrade_plan: Upgrade strategy uses dual-write and staged rotation: (A) Add a new key handle in HSM, (B) configure dual-write where new writes go to both old and new key until verification passes, (C) re-encrypt a small set of secrets and verify reads, (D) cutover after verification, (E) retire old key after TTL. Terraform changes that touch key handles should be guarded behind a tfvar flag 'allow_key_rotation=true' and run with an approval step in the CI pipeline.
testing_plan: Unit tests for TF module (tftest) validate input validation and plan-only checks
Integration job in CI that spins a minimal VPC staging cluster, attaches HSM emulator, deploys Vault and secrets-sync controller, runs end-to-end scenarios
Chaos test that simulates HSM connectivity loss and verifies controller's retry/backoff and SRE alerts
Security test where state file and remote state access attempts are simulated to ensure no plain key material is leaked
risks: Misconfiguration could lead to dual-write divergence between cloud secrets and Vault
Terraform state leakage if customers misuse 'export_key_material' flag; mitigated by explicit deny and CI gating
HSM vendor idiosyncrasies require provider shims; initial implementation supports two vendors and falls back to cloud-kms shim
Migration complexity for existing on-prem Vault users with pre-existing unwrapped secrets
